subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the production zone to search for Lyney

40080203.text: Did you two run into any trouble over the past few days?

40080204.text: No, we just worked our shifts according to the schedule. Nothing weird happened.

40080205.text: Mmm, that's good. That means you didn't raise any suspicions when you infiltrated the infirmary.

40080206.text: We've taken a look at the slip you've sent. Freminet successfully left the grounds via the pipes two days ago, and as of last night, Lynette has also infiltrated the infirmary after faking an illness.

40080207.text: Wait, why is she getting involved as well?

40080208.text: You already went above and beyond when you scoped out the infirmary. To put it more bluntly, even if we were to view that as something you did in exchange for Freminet's help, you've already done more than enough.

40080209.text: Infiltrating a guarded stronghold is a different kind of job from a one-off investigation. We want to avoid using the same faces over and over, and reduce the amount of suspicion that will fall on any given person.

40080210.text: Lynette also felt like you have already taken the first step for us, so she should be the one to finish the job.

40080211.text: So that's what Lynette thinks... Paimon hopes everything's going well for her.

40080220.text: Then... Let's go check on Lynette before Freminet returns. If everything went well, then she should be wrapping up her investigation right about now.

40080221.text: Is now really a good time to go over?

40080222.text: According to my observations, Sigewinne always spends around half an hour away from the infirmary right before lunch. Lynette knows this as well, so this should be a good time to meet up with her.

40080223.text: Oh yeah, we heard about that too.

40080224.text: Also, I'm her brother, remember? It's only natural for an older brother to care about his younger sister's well-being.

40080225.text: Okay, then let's head over right away!

40080214.text: Perhaps that's true. You are both very good people, and we've come to appreciate that more than anyone else. Unfortunately, there's still one thing that could get between us, lest you've forgotten... The matter of our respective loyalties.

40080215.text: You've mentioned before that you've had some run-ins with the Fatui. I can understand that feeling, so I assume you're just helping us out of the kindness of your hearts?

40080216.text: Well, everyone could use some more friends! We'll be counting on you to help us in the future too.

40080217.text: Mhm. Since I see you as friends, then it's even more important for us to protect you from any peril. Freminet and Lynette feel the same way.

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the Infirmary in secret

40080301.text: Lynette should be here right now...

40080304.text: As expected, Sigewinne isn't here, but... why isn't Lynette here?

40080307.text: ...No, Lynette rarely deviates from the plan. We agreed that if she were to make changes on the fly, she'd find a way to let me know.

40080309.text: Let's see if there are any clues around here, we can look while we wait for her. Who knows, maybe she'll be back soon!

subQuests.subQuestName: Search for clues in the Infirmary

40080401.text: There are some books here, and a few files... They all look like medical records.

40080402.text: Hmm... "Advanced Nursing," "How to Raise the Spirits of Your Patients," "A Quick Guide to the Psychology of Emotions," and "The Meaning of Laughter"...

40080403.text: These sure are some interesting books... Who knew Sigewinne would be interested in these kinds of things...

40080404.text: She even has books on understanding people's motivations and feelings... Is it because she's a Melusine? Or does she have a need to understand her patients' emotional state?

40080405.text: Seems quite normal to me. These are skills that would come in handy for a nurse from time to time.

subQuests.subQuestName: Search for clues in the Infirmary

40080501.text: Ah, this is it, we saw it before!

40080502.text: Wait, this thing...? It doesn't look like it's been disguised that well.

40080503.text: Lyney leans down to get close to the movable hatch, and starts tapping at several different points on it...

40080504.text: The space behind it is empty. From its size, I don't think it's an entrance that is meant to be taken apart. There's probably a mechanism around here somewhere.

40080505.text: Could Lynette have tried to get inside? But if that's the case, she would have contacted me for sure...

40080507.text: Let's look around here some more for clues... Don't panic, just... take another look.

40080508.text: (The look on Lyney's face... He's definitely beginning to panic. "Don't panic"... He probably said that subconsciously more for himself than anything else.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Search for clues in the Infirmary

40080601.text: None of the beds have any signs of having been slept in... except that one over there.

40080602.text: That's the one Lynette must have used, right? You said she was pretending to be sick.

40080603.text: Mhm. She would have said her migraine was having a particularly bad flare-up. Generally speaking, the head nurse would then ask her to lie down and rest, while she left to retrieve the medication.

40080605.text: Which means, either the head nurse didn't return the entire time from when Lynette lay down up until she left the bed, or... the nurse intentionally left it this way.

40080606.text: (Oh no... That's not a good sign...)

40080701.text: Hey, you guys, there's a slip of paper over here!

40080703.text: It's right over here, and there's a bunch written on it, too... It reads...

40080704.text: "Out of respect for your usual practices, I'll use a piece of paper or card as the medium to pass on my message. You may consider this as me giving you my best regards."

40080707.text: Is there anything on the back?

40080708.text: The back... aaah! This... This is...

40080711.text: Th—That look on your face... P—Paimon's reading it now...

40080712.text: "Would you care to guess where Miss Lynette of the Fatui could be right now?"

40080713.text: ...No... Could she have... Is she already...

40080714.text: ...Wriothesley... Did he deliberately leave the infirmary unguarded to use it as bait?

40080715.text: Wait, you mean... He was aware of our goals from the very beginning? But why? We didn't run into any trouble last time, and he also never reached out to us since...

40080716.text: Why would he choose to act during our second infiltration attempt instead of the first?

40080717.text: ...Yes, that is a crucial question. Wriothesley... He doesn't do anything without a clear goal or reason. So, this means he had no concerns about your activities from the very beginning.

40080718.text: #{NICKNAME}, you are not from the same camp as us — you were sent down here by Neuvillette, so you have no conflict of interest with Wriothesley. We're a completely different story, though...

40080721.text: I'd like to know that, too. Why did he only go after her?

40080722.text: Don't panic, just think everything over... I have to stay calm... This is not like what happened last time, the situation's different now...

40080724.text: #{NICKNAME}, wait, you're right... Wait... But that means...

40080725.text: ...The fact that Freminet was able to leave the grounds... Could Wriothesley have let him go as well?

40080726.text: But what does he gain by letting Freminet leave like that?

40080728.text: He deliberately made them both disappear.

40080729.text: ...So he's challenging me and trying to provoke me. I'm sure of it.

40080730.text: Ugh, we never should have sent out Freminet! We had to go through all that trouble to find an opening to sneak him around the guards and into the pipe, and we even thought luck was on our side...

40080731.text: If Wriothesley let him leave on purpose... Then he's probably in a terrible spot now as well...

40080732.text: Lyney's getting more and more panicked... We have to calm him down!

40080734.text: Don't be like this, Lyney. Freminet wouldn't have left if we hadn't told you about Childe... That was our fault...

40080735.text: No, I'm the leader of this operation, and I'm the one responsible for this team... I was the one who failed to protect them.

40080737.text: #Hey, don't be reckless! {NICKNAME}, please talk some sense into him!

40080738.text: I simply cannot allow Lynette to be abducted again...

40080739.text: I have to go, I'll find a way to get them back!

40080740.text: He's rushed out the door! After him!

40080742.text: Right, I feel like we still have some room to make changes on these details.

40080743.text: ...It's not impossible, but it'll require extensive testing.

40080744.text: Is that so... Very well, then please be mindful of the time.

40080748.text: ...Whoever's outside is eavesdropping. They'll probably come in once we stop talking.

40080751.text: (Ah, these two. As expected, they've already found this place. They're quite sharp.)

40080752.text: What a delightful turn of events. I like smart people, but I also like playing dumb. I like the feeling of "being trusted."

40080753.text: Oh my! What's wrong, little one? There's no need to panic — take a deep breath before you begin.

40080754.text: Being able to read human expressions is quite the useful skill.

subQuests.subQuestName: Check the piece of paper on the ground
Catch up with Lyney

40080901.text: Ooh, close one. I owe you, Sigewinne. That was a fantastic shot.

40080904.text: Though this gun may look like a toy, it's actually fully functional, as I just demonstrated.

40080906.text: Are you his accomplice in all this!?

40080907.text: Not at all. I am merely a resident of the Fortress, and thus protecting it is my duty.

40080908.text: When Monsieur Neuvillette asked me to come here, he told me that my job would be to take care of the well-being of everyone here. I am merely discharging my duties.

40080909.text: But if you mean what you just said, then isn't Lyney someone you should be looking after as well? Isn't he a resident here just like the rest of us?

40080912.text: But I really am just doing what Monsieur Neuvillette told me to do! Everything I did, I've done to protect them. Had I not, they would be in far more dire straits right now.

40080913.text: His Grace knows it, too. Right? Your Grace? ...Mind proving my innocence to them?

40080914.text: ...*sigh* My dear Sigewinne, what ever shall I do with you? Would it have killed you to just wait another minute or two?

40080915.text: Well, it's nearly time, after all. The way you do things can be truly frustrating sometimes, Your Grace. I figured I should try to talk some sense into you.

40080916.text: What are you talking about? What time?

40080917.text: Take me if you want... But let them go...

40080918.text: How touching. Can you just give me one more minute?

40080919.text: Don't be like that, Your Grace.

40080920.text: Alright, everyone, calm down. Two more visitors will be arriving any time now.

40080921.text: I will go get a cup of tea. Miss Sigewinne, I'll leave Miss Lynette in your care.

40080924.text: The door suddenly slams open. A familiar figure bursts into the room.

40080929.text: What's going on!? What is Clorinde doing here?

40080931.text: I'm sorry about shooting you, Mr. Lyney. The tranquilizing effect will begin to wear off soon. Please take it easy in the meantime, though.

40080932.text: ...What happened to Freminet? Wasn't he diving just outside of the fortress? Why is he looking like... Like this...

40080934.text: A flushed face and accelerated pulse... He must have consumed Primordial Seawater.

40080936.text: Please make some space. I'll need to give Mr. Freminet a more thorough check-up. Your Grace, I'll leave the rest to you.

40080937.text: I'll talk to Clorinde while you get Freminet to where he needs to be. Everything else can wait.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Duke's Office

40080801.text: Come out and face me, Wriothesley!

40080802.text: Mmm, aren't we at an administrative office space? Why don't you at least try to follow even a couple rules from the Fortress' Indoor Management Regulations?

40080803.text: What did you do to my sister!?

40080804.text: I ran into the young miss at the infirmary. I had heard that she was suffering from quite the migraine, so I decided to invite her over for a cup of tea. I do have some teas in my collection that can work wonders against such an illness.

40080805.text: Stop joking around! Where did you take my siblings!?

40080806.text: I have also heard that your performances are quite the spectacle. Miss Lynette would sometimes enter a box filled with water, only to emerge the next second from another place altogether.

40080807.text: Maybe she'll appear behind you right now if you were to turn your head?

40080808.text: (Is he trying to trick me into turning my head? No, he's probably not looking to attack me right now, all of the hostages are in his hands, and he's even in the mood for small talk. That means Lynette is probably still alive.)

40080809.text: #...You knew we were investigating the infirmary from the start, so you deliberately aroused {NICKNAME}'s suspicions and baited us into continuing our investigation, just so that you'd be able to kidnap Lynette.

40080811.text: As for Freminet... No, you probably didn't even interfere with Childe's escape. You let him go, so you could purge the Fatui members that we had planted into your ranks.

40080812.text: There was no need to do so. The Fortress of Meropide is a pretty pleasant place. Most people enjoy their lives here — the only ones who act differently are those with personal agendas. It was quite easy to identify your colleagues.

40080813.text: You removed our original members, and spread the news of Childe's escape, so "Father" would assign our team to come down and investigate. Freminet has also fallen into your hands, right? If you're oh so omnipotent and so in control, why would you need hostages?

40080814.text: One correction. Lynette is in my hands right now, but Freminet is not.

40080815.text: He's not? ...What do you really want?

40080817.text: Oh, wonderful! Everyone is here, so I'll only need to say this once: thank you so much for cooperating with me.

40080819.text: #Eager and to the point, {NICKNAME}, I see. Alas, only Miss Lynette is currently having a cup of the Fortress' finest tea.

40080820.text: Although as per your original plan, Mr. Freminet should also have returned to the Fortress by now. But he has neither shown up within my gates, nor has he been taken into any kind of custody. So where do you think he may be right now...?

40080822.text: You locked him outside in the sea!?

40080823.text: I closed the Fortress' gate to the outside world, that's all.

40080824.text: Freminet's a star diver, so he should be fine, right?

40080825.text: No, we're still here, so he'd definitely try to find a way to come back for us... So we can't assume he might have made a break for the surface.

40080826.text: But why would I do this, you may be asking? To have an audience with you, of course. My intel tells me that Mr. Lyney is a great magician, so it's only natural for me to want to have some cards of my own when it comes to negotiating.

40080827.text: Besides, I do recall you mentioning to Miss Lynette that you've always wanted to have a face-to-face meeting with the lord of the Fortress of Meropide, regardless of whether it was in a personal or a professional capacity. Well you got your wish.

40080828.text: So... You've been keeping tabs on us before we even set foot in the Fortress...

40080829.text: Some of my folks just happened to hear a thing or two, that's all. In any case, I'll be straight with you.

40080830.text: I was willing to play dumb and turn a blind eye, so we had a pleasant few days playing games together here. But once you started focusing on the "forbidden zone," all of that changed.

40080831.text: Mr. Lyney, the cards are stacked against you right now. Miss Lynette is in my hands, and Mr. Freminet is still slowly being pickled out there in the brine. You know just as well as I that he cannot last out there forever.

40080832.text: You need do but one thing to guarantee their safety. I would like you to contact your superior, and ideally invite her over for a cup of tea with me.

40080833.text: You want to see "Father"? Ha, but why should she bother giving you an audience?

40080834.text: Well, if she cares for the well-being of her dearest children, she should have plenty of motivation to join me for a parents' evening.

40080835.text: I've heard that the bonds between the members of the House of the Hearth are like the bonds of family. I don't see why she would refuse.

40080836.text: Why did you think "Father" sent us to handle the Fortress of Meropide? This place is basically a no man's land. It wouldn't be fitting for anyone as important as a Harbinger like "Father" to come here in person.

40080837.text: Oh, I see, so it's because she doesn't care for my place here. That's such a shame, after all, I've amassed quite the tea collection, and I was looking forward to sharing it with her. Both Monsieur Neuvillette and Lady Furina have already received many samples as gifts.

40080838.text: ...Was this the extent of your master plan to get to "Father"? No matter how much pressure you may put on me, I won't allow you to use us to blackmail her.

40080839.text: Your people really are difficult to get along with. All I'm asking for is a face-to-face conversation. Does she truly have no interest in the Fortress' secret?

40080840.text: Mr. Lyney, you have one last chance to invite your "Father" here. If you refuse...

40080843.text: Why do you have to do this?

40080844.text: Instead of asking why I'm doing this, why don't you try to see things from my perspective for a second? From the very beginning, the Fatui has been actively infiltrating my Fortress.

40080845.text: I gave you a warning by cutting off the first few operatives I found, but that only caused you to double down. Had you given up on the Fortress then and there, I'd have no reason to want a talk.

40080846.text: Mr. Freminet left the Fortress on his own, and Miss Lynette tried to pry out my secrets right in front of me. No matter how you look at it, the responsibility for this falls on you.

40080847.text: I... I shouldn't ask "Father" to do anything because of us...

40080851.text: Time's up. It really is a shame, Mr. Lyney.

40080853.text: Negotiations have broken down. Please leave, ladies and gentlemen. It's time for my afternoon tea.

40080855.text: Please wait! Can we really not talk about this some more?

40080856.text: #Yeah, listen to {NICKNAME}! If you can't talk to Lyney, can you at least talk to us?

40080857.text: You do realize that I'm only letting you go because of Neuvillette, yes? You're here helping him out, and I've already done my best to stay out of your way.

40080858.text: But that doesn't mean you can just do whatever you want. The Fortress may be small and remote, but it still has its own set of laws.

40080862.text: Then how about this? Those who are capable deserve respect. You've spent quite some time investigating my home turf by now, so why don't you tell me a thing or two about what you've found?

40080863.text: I'll ask you three questions. Answer all of them correctly, and I'll agree to your request.

40080864.text: Question one. Regarding the "hidden rules" of the production zone... What is the truth behind the one about not being allowed to work for three days in a row?

40080865.text: (I can't believe he's asking about the "hidden rules"... If I recall correctly, if you keep working without any rest, during lunch hour on the third day, you will find a portion of "strange meat" in your welfare meal.)

40080866.text: (It's a good thing that we've already run a thorough investigation on this. Let's see if I can remember all the clues... I should be able to find an answer if I can piece everything together.)

40080867.text: Ah, so that's what was going on... Paimon understands it now. Who would have guessed...

40080868.text: The "hidden rule" of the production zone... people are not supposed to work three days in a row, and if they do, they'll get "strange meat" in their welfare meal.

40080869.text: At first, we thought this "strange meat" must have something to do with the people who disappeared, but in reality, they were all... prepared by Sigewinne, the head nurse.

40080870.text: She often visits the production zone to observe the workers' health, and makes a note of anyone who has worn themselves out after three full days of work.

40080871.text: Out of her sense of duty as the head nurse as well as her genuine concern for the workers' health, Sigewinne visits the cafeteria right before lunch, and cooks an "extra dish" for those who can use the stamina boost.

40080872.text: Sigewinne has only the best intentions with her "surprise gift," and doesn't want anyone to find out about what she does. However...

40080873.text: ...Unfortunately, Melusines as a race perceive the world differently from humans, and their sense of aesthetics is even more alien to us.

40080874.text: The recipients of her lovingly prepared special meals cannot taste the care within, and usually just freak out.

40080875.text: Are we on the right track?

40080876.text: Heh, not bad. You've uncovered Sigewinne's secret, and even guessed her intentions correctly as well. It's nice to know that her efforts have not gone unacknowledged.

40080877.text: Alright, now for my next question...

40080878.text: There are also some "hidden rules" in the Pankration Ring... Including the one that you're not allowed to support both sides of a fight. Why is that?

40080879.text: (The "hidden rules" of the Pankration Ring... I remember. If someone tries to support both boxers at the same time, they'll receive a package the next morning, which contains a strange blood-colored liquid.)

40080880.text: (We've also done a lot of research on this matter. Let me sift through what I've found and come up with the correct answer.)

40080881.text: Ah, Paimon gets this rule too now... So there really was nothing to be afraid of!

40080882.text: That "hidden rule" of the Pankration Ring is about how... people are not supposed to bet on both boxers at the same time, and if they do, they'll receive a package containing a strange blood-colored liquid.

40080883.text: People get scared when they see it because they've subconsciously begun to associate it with the missing boxer.

40080884.text: But really, it's just a bottle of the latest yet-to-be-named-and-packaged new Fonta trial product!

40080885.text: A blood-red drink... It's no wonder even Fonta's own staff were questioning the company's decision-making.

40080886.text: The company, facing backlash from its own staff, decided to try to trial the product on a smaller scale, to see how it might be received by customers.

40080887.text: They came to the Fortress of Meropide and offered to sponsor the Pankration tournament so they could push their new product, but the Duke completely refused to even entertain the idea.

40080888.text: The Duke, knowing how valuable coupons are in the Fortress, knew that only total idiots who didn't understand their true value would bother buying a Fonta product here.

40080889.text: And so, only those who proved their stupidity by being dumb enough to bet on two opposing sides of the same match were selected to receive the drinks.

40080890.text: I acknowledge the effort you've put in to bringing the truth of this mystery to light.

40080891.text: Although, based on your description, that Fonta promoter is a bit too careless with his words... I may just reconsider my collaboration with the company.

40080892.text: Alright, and here's the final question. What's the secret behind our head nurse, and all of her patients in the infirmary?

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to understand the situation of the people around

40081002.text: (Lyney's expression looks disgusted... It seems like he'd rather not have Sigewinne touch Freminet. Still, he didn't stop her, since it's obvious that Freminet does require urgent medical care.)

40081003.text: (Sigewinne's examining Freminet carefully. She doesn't look too upset, which is a good sign. I hope Freminet will be okay.)

40081005.text: These symptoms are probably caused by an acute ingestion of a large amount of Primordial Seawater. Still, his condition is not critical.

40081006.text: Of course, it would be best if he stayed for further observation. Let's leave him here for now, and move him to the infirmary once he's recovered a bit more.

40081007.text: ...Sorry, I am aware that the infirmary may not be your favorite place in the world at the moment. We do only have a single clinic in the fortress, however.

40081009.text: ...Why would he ingest a large amount of Primordial Seawater after leaving the Fortress? How could that possibly happen...?

40081010.text: Please look after Mr. Freminet for the moment. I'll go fetch some medicine and a respirator. I'll bring Miss Lynette back with me.

40081011.text: Where is she!? How is she right now!?

40081012.text: Oh, she just took a nap in an empty room after I tranquilized her. If my calculations are correct, she should also be waking up right around now. You might not believe me, but His Grace and I actually made some snacks and tea for her.

40081013.text: (Lyney has finally begun to stop tensing the muscles on his face. It seems that he trusts what Sigewinne just said.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to understand the situation of the people around

40081101.text: What's that look on your face? I thought I made good time on the way back.

40081102.text: Oh, I'm just admiring your punctuality. Had you arrived just a few minutes later, Sigewinne may have been forced to shoot Mr. Lyney again.

40081104.text: The water has changed. It's pretty much as expected. The concentration of Primordial Seawater has increased significantly.

40081105.text: I was only out there a short time, so it wasn't too bad. But if one were to stay for any significant amount of time... Well, you can see how that boy is doing.

40081106.text: Where was he when you found him?

40081107.text: The abandoned zone at the end of the pipes. A good distance into the water.

40081108.text: Closer than I thought. He must have recognized it early on, and tried desperately to swim back.

40081109.text: Locking the door was necessary. I don't think we could have saved two.

40081110.text: Well, I did try to convince them that I had my reasons... Never seems to work, though.

40081111.text: It would probably work on Neuvillette. He has a knack for picking out who had good intentions even when the outcomes were all terrible.

40081112.text: Eh... It's a bad sign if you're having to plead your case to Neuvillette.

40081114.text: Not particularly. If you want to drink some that badly, just say so.

40081115.text: Fine, I'd like to get some tea. Want me to get you a cup too, since I've already made it?

40081116.text: Eh, might as well then, I suppose. Actually, do you have a towel? I would like to dry my hair.

40081302.text: He's awake. Freminet, how do you feel?

40081306.text: The infirmary at the Fortress of Meropide, Mr. Freminet, and you are no longer in any danger.

40081307.text: How do you feel? Don't push yourself if you're not feeling up to it!

40081309.text: ...The sea! There's something wrong with the seawater!

40081310.text: Shh, it's okay. We can talk about it after you've recovered.

40081311.text: No, listen to me, this is really serious! There's Primordial Seawater mixed into the regular seawater. I don't know why it's there, but no one should touch it!

40081312.text: What happened after you snuck into the pipes?

40081314.text: ...Right, the pipes. It's all coming back to me now...

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Lyney

40081202.text: ...I'll be fine. They're all here now. Don't worry about me.

40081203.text: Are you sure? You don't look alright...

40081204.text: My hands and feet are still a bit weak, but that's probably just the residual effects of the tranquilizer shot.

40081208.text: He'll be fine. But for now, please help me lift him up.

40081209.text: Lyney and Lynette immediately come to lift Freminet up. With their help, Freminet also manages to swallow a dose of Sigewinne's medicine.

40081211.text: His breathing's beginning to slow down.

40081212.text: Give me a hand and help me get him to the infirmary.

40081213.text: Yeah, I'll take him from this side. Lynette? Together?

40081215.text: #{NICKNAME}, you seem pretty worried about him. Want to come with us?

40081217.text: The Duke and Clorinde are gone...

40081218.text: They probably went to get some tea. The Duke will explain the truth in just a bit. Miss Clorinde will need a break, since she only just returned from rescuing Freminet out of the sea.

40081219.text: (Clorinde saved Freminet from the sea... Just what happened there?)

subQuests.subQuestName: Go back to the Infirmary with Freminet
Talk to Freminet
Explore the Unknown Area

40081501.text: ...I'm in. Hmm... Seems like this pipe hasn't been used in a long time. It looks abandoned.

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for clues concerning Childe

40081601.text: This is where the water starts... Okay.

40081602.text: (Master Childe probably dived into the water... I'll go take a look as well.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Dive into the water to continue your investigation

40081702.text: (My heart is racing, and it's getting harder and harder to breathe. What's going on?)

40081703.text: (No good, I have to get back, they still don't know anything about what's going on! If I turn back right now, I should still be able to make it...)

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to shore quickly

40081802.text: (This is... This is bad... I'm feeling worse and worse... And I'm still underwater...)

40082201.text: Could I tempt you with some sugar for your tea?

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Lyney

40081901.text: ...So, in other words, the trail you were following vanished, and you had no idea where Master Childe could have gone, but there was also no obvious place for him to have disappeared to...

40081902.text: That's right. I tried my best to swim back, but I had already put some distance between myself and the fortress, and I just couldn't find the strength to keep going... I probably passed out sometime after that, and you know the rest.

40081903.text: Miss Clorinde brought you back, but we also don't know why she just suddenly appeared at the Fortress, or why she went out to save you...

40081904.text: Miss Clorinde, you say... I must go thank her in person.

40081905.text: You're still too weak, Freminet. You can go after you've had some more rest.

40081906.text: Miss Lynette is right. I believe Miss Clorinde will stay here as a guest for another few days, so there's no need to hurry.

40081907.text: A guest... Then I can assume Wriothesley was the one who invited her to come down here?

40081908.text: You should ask His Grace about that. He'll be able to explain better than me.

40081909.text: Got it, I'll go talk to him.

40081910.text: Yeah, it's about time he actually told us what's going on! Wanna come with us, Lyney?

40081912.text: #No, please go on without me, {NICKNAME}. I don't want to leave just yet.

40081914.text: ...The logical part of my brain is aware that we are safe right now, but I still can't bring myself to leave. Both of you were just in danger.

40081915.text: Understood. Then let's just sit together for a while.

40081916.text: #In that case, I'll leave the infirmary to you. {NICKNAME} and I are going to head out for now — as long as you stay in here, I don't think you'll be disturbed.

subQuests.subQuestName: Additional
Additional

40089903.text: He's already out of sight, how is he so fast... Let's go head him off at Wriothesley's office!

40089904.text: (We often see Miss Sigewinne observing the prisoners at work near the production zone. It seems like she can perceive the general state of a person's health just by looking at them.)

40089905.text: #(The research notes said that the Melusine race perceives the world very differently from humans. {M#As a result}{F#Because of that}, the Melusines have also developed a sense of aesthetics that appears rather strange and alien to humans.)

40089906.text: (I've been told that the infirmary is always empty for the half hour just before lunch. But what could Sigewinne be doing during that time?)

40089907.text: (According to Collins, the pankration tournament only took place because the Fonta company sponsored it. The company must want a return on their investment as well.)

40089908.text: (Fonta's internal reports suggest that they're starting a new trial of an unnamed and unpackaged product. But the product has to undergo a trial because even Fonta's own employees have a lot of reservations about it.)

40089909.text: (The Fonta promoter has been struggling because he doesn't recognize the real value of coupons. Meanwhile, the Duke believes that only idiots who don't understand the value of coupons will spend them on Fonta.)

40089911.text: (The vegetation here is a bit more sparse... These traces aren't natural, a person must have left them, and recently. I should be going in the right direction.)

40089912.text: (There are traces here, too. I need to keep going.)

40089913.text: (Eh? The traces are gone? But I don't see where he could have gone from here...)

40089914.text: (If you break the hidden rule of the Production Zone, your Welfare Meal might contain some strange meat...)

40089915.speakerName: A Package Containing Strange Blood-Colored Fluid
40089915.text: (If you violate the hidden rules of the Pankration Ring, you will receive a bag containing a strange blood-colored fluid.)

40089916.text: (Sigewinne often observes the people working at the Production Zone.)

40089917.text: (The infirmary is often empty in the afternoon. This is likely related to Sigewinne's absence during this time.)

40089918.speakerName: Research About the Characteristics of Melusines
40089918.text: (A Melusine's sense of sight differs from a human's. Melusines don't find this too strange.)

40089919.text: (This is most likely the sponsor of the Pankration Tournament.)

40089920.text: (The Duke believes that only idiots who don't appreciate the value of a coupon will spend them on the Fonta being sold by any promoters.)

40089921.text: (Fonta Co.'s as-yet unnamed or packaged new drink is being promoted for the first time, but some employees have their doubts about it.)
